text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- The National Bank of Poland, the central bank, decided to sell two banks it now controls, Polish Investment Bank (PBI) and ailing Prosper Bank, to Kredyt Bank, sources said. This means that the central bank rejected bids from Austria's Creditanstalt and General Electric Capital
- The Szczecin shipyard has increased its stake in Tuk insurance company to 92 percent from the earlier 81 percent by buying up shares from Tuk's minority shareholders.

- Bank Pekao SA is likely to grant the Gdansk shipyard, which has been operating under bankruptcy rules and began laying off workers last month, a loan that will enable it to resume work on a vessel for a German shipowner.

- The level of public confidence in leading Polish politicians has fallen since January, a CBOS survey showed. The politician enjoying the greatest public trust is the opposition Union for Freedom's Jacek Kuron, who is trusted by 68 percent of Poles.

Kuron is followed by two politicians linked with the governing coalition -- lower house of parliament speaker Josef Zych of the Polish Peasants Party (PSL), with 65 percent, and President Aleksander Kwasniewski, a former leader of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), with 62 percent.
